result.rationale: Diff shows `blacklistedGuestEmails = ...map((email) => email.toLowerCase())` but the check is `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` with un-normalized guest; likewise `guest === attendee.email` is case-sensitive. Both mechanisms are verifiably present in addGuests.handler.ts, so uppercase emails bypass the blacklist and duplicates can be created.

judged_text: Blacklist entries are lowercased but the guest address is compared verbatim (blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)) and the existing-attendee check is case-sensitive (guest === attendee.email), so both guards are defeated by case variation. Submitting USER@EXAMPLE.COM bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entirely, and A@x.com plus a@x.com both pass the filter and create two attendee rows for the same person.
